1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 d5 5.Nf3.strategy: Develops a piece and prepares to castle before settling the tension on c4 and d5. White keeps more options than with an immediate capture, at the price of leaving Black to choose whether to take on c4 or to keep the pawn on d5.
1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 d5 5.Nf3.name: Neo-Grünfeld Defence: with g3

1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 d5 5.cxd.strategy: Resolves the tension at once and leaves the recapturing knight exposed in the centre to the bishop on g2 and to a possible e-pawn push. White gets a freer, open game and a simple plan: build the centre while Black looks for counterplay.

The natural recapture: the knight reaches the centre, covered by the queen. Black gets quick development and an active game, but the knight is attacked by the bishop on g2 and can be driven off by a central pawn push.

1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 d5 5.Nf3.strategy: Brings the king to safety before the centre opens and puts the rook on f8. With the king secure Black can handle the tension on c4 and d5 calmly, whichever way White resolves it.
